buildNotes: Every seesaw access is a write of two bytes, module base then function register; for a read wait a few ms, then read the bytes back, big-endian.
Encoder position: base 0x11, register 0x30, 4 bytes, signed 32-bit, one count per detent. Register 0x40 is the delta since the last read.

The knob's switch is seesaw GPIO pin 24: set it input with pull-up (DIRCLR_BULK 0x01 0x03, PULLENSET 0x01 0x0B, BULK_SET 0x01 0x05, mask 1<<24), then read GPIO_BULK (0x01 0x04, 4 bytes); bit 24 reads 0 while pressed.
Default address 0x36; close A0/A1/A2 on the back to add 1/2/4 (up to 0x3D) for several encoders on one bus.
The encoder itself is soldered by you on product 4991 (any PEC11-style encoder with switch); product 5880 comes with it fitted.
On-board NeoPixel is on seesaw pin 6 (not used by this driver).

driver.code:
# Adafruit I2C QT Rotary Encoder (product 4991, seesaw firmware), MicroPython driver.
# seesaw protocol: every access starts with a write of [module base, function register];
# for a read, wait briefly, then read the bytes back (all values big-endian).
import time

_STATUS_BASE = 0x00
_STATUS_HW_ID = 0x01
_STATUS_SWRST = 0x7F
_GPIO_BASE = 0x01
_GPIO_DIRCLR_BULK = 0x03
_GPIO_BULK = 0x04
_GPIO_BULK_SET = 0x05
_GPIO_PULLENSET = 0x0B
_ENCODER_BASE = 0x11
_ENCODER_POSITION = 0x30
_ENCODER_DELTA = 0x40

_HW_IDS = (0x55, 0x84, 0x85, 0x86, 0x87, 0x88, 0x89)  # SAMD09 (this board) and ATtiny8xx/16xx seesaw chips
_BUTTON_PIN = 24  # seesaw pin of the encoder's push switch on this board


class SeesawEncoder:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x36, reset=True):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if reset:
            self._write(_STATUS_BASE, _STATUS_SWRST, b'\xff')
            time.sleep_ms(500)  # seesaw restarts after a software reset
        hw = self._read(_STATUS_BASE, _STATUS_HW_ID, 1)[0]
        if hw not in _HW_IDS:
            raise OSError('seesaw not found at 0x%02x (HW_ID 0x%02x): check the wiring' % (addr, hw))
        # Encoder switch: input with pull-up (pressed pulls it to GND).
        mask = (1 << _BUTTON_PIN).to_bytes(4, 'big')
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_DIRCLR_BULK, mask)
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_PULLENSET, mask)
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_BULK_SET, mask)

    def _write(self, base, reg, data=b''):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([base, reg]) + bytes(data))

    def _read(self, base, reg, n, delay_us=8000):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([base, reg]))
        time.sleep_us(delay_us)  # seesaw needs time to fetch the value before the read
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, n)

    @staticmethod
    def _int32(b):
        v = (b[0] << 24) | (b[1] << 16) | (b[2] << 8) | b[3]
        return v - (1 << 32) if v & 0x80000000 else v

    def position(self):
        """Encoder position in detents (signed 32-bit counter kept by seesaw)."""
        return self._int32(self._read(_ENCODER_BASE, _ENCODER_POSITION, 4))

    def set_position(self, pos):
        self._write(_ENCODER_BASE, _ENCODER_POSITION, (pos & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, 'big'))

    def delta(self):
        """Detents turned since the last delta() call (reading clears it)."""
        return self._int32(self._read(_ENCODER_BASE, _ENCODER_DELTA, 4))

    def pressed(self):
        """True while the encoder knob is pushed in."""
        b = self._read(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_BULK, 4)
        bits = (b[0] << 24) | (b[1] << 16) | (b[2] << 8) | b[3]
        return not (bits >> _BUTTON_PIN) & 1

# Adafruit I2C QT Rotary Encoder (Adafruit 4991)

## Overview
A rotary encoder with a push switch, read over I2C. An **ATSAMD09** running Adafruit's **seesaw** firmware counts the detents in a signed 32-bit position and reads the knob's switch, so you only need SDA and SCL. It has two STEMMA QT / Qwiic sockets, an on-board NeoPixel on seesaw pin 6, and a 3.3 V regulator with level-shifted I2C. On product 4991 you solder the encoder yourself (any PEC11-style encoder with a switch). Product 5880 is the same board with the encoder already fitted.

## Pinout (header order, as printed on the board)
| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| VIN | Supply, 3-5 V (use the same voltage as your board's logic) |
| 3Vo | 3.3 V regulator output, up to 100 mA (leave unconnected) |
| GND | Ground |
| SCL | I2C clock (10 k pull-up on board) |
| SDA | I2C data (10 k pull-up on board) |
| INT | Interrupt output, active low (optional; it must be enabled in seesaw) |

## Electrical limits
- Supply: 3-5 V on VIN. The AP2112K regulator feeds the SAMD09 with 3.3 V.
- The I2C lines are level-shifted (BSS138), so 3.3 V and 5 V logic are both fine.
- Current: a few mA, plus up to about 20 mA more when the NeoPixel is lit.

## Interface details
- **I2C address 0x36** by default. Closing the A0/A1/A2 jumpers on the back adds 1/2/4, giving up to 0x3D.
- The seesaw protocol: write `[module base, function register]` with any data after it. To read, write the two bytes, wait (the driver waits 8 ms, as Adafruit's CircuitPython library does), then read. Values are big-endian.
- STATUS base 0x00: HW_ID 0x01 reads **0x55** on this SAMD09 board. SWRST 0x7F: write 0xFF, then wait about 500 ms.
- ENCODER base 0x11: POSITION 0x30 is a signed 32-bit count of detents (you can also write it to set the count). DELTA 0x40 is the change since its last read, and reading it clears it.
- Switch: seesaw GPIO pin 24. Set it up with DIRCLR_BULK (0x01 0x03), PULLENSET (0x01 0x0B) and BULK_SET (0x01 0x05), each with the mask 1<<24. Then read GPIO_BULK (0x01 0x04, 4 bytes). Bit 24 reads 0 while the knob is pressed.

## Wiring
- ESP32: VIN → 3V3, GND → GND, SDA → D21, SCL → D22.
- Pico: VIN → 3V3(OUT), GND → GND, SDA → GP4, SCL → GP5.
- Raspberry Pi 4: VIN → pin 1 (3.3 V), GND → pin 6, SDA → pin 3, SCL → pin 5.
- You can also use a STEMMA QT / Qwiic cable instead of the header.

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
from seesaw_encoder import SeesawEncoder
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22))
enc = SeesawEncoder(i2c)          # address 0x36
print(enc.position(), enc.pressed())
```

## Gotchas
- Always leave a short delay between the register write and the read. Reading too quickly returns stale or garbage bytes.
- Direction: Adafruit's CircuitPython example negates the position so that clockwise counts up. Flip the sign in your code if it turns the wrong way.
- In the Sparkbench simulator, the slider sets the POSITION register. DELTA is not modelled, so use `position()` there.
- Several encoders on one bus: give each board its own address with the A0-A2 jumpers.

## Datasheet
- SAMD09 (the chip): https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/Atmel-42414-SAM-D09_Datasheet.pdf
- Board guide: https://learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-i2c-qt-rotary-encoder
